title: Minimum Time to Activate String
summary: Given a string s of length n and an integer array order , where order is a permutation of the numbers in the range [0, n - 1], replace the character at index order[t] in s with '*' at each time step t .
statement: Given a string s of length n and an integer array order , where order is a permutation of the numbers in the range [0, n - 1], replace the character at index order[t] in s with '*' at each time step t . A substring is considered valid if it contains at least one '*'. The string is deemed active if the total number of valid substrings is at least k . Return the minimum time t at which the string s becomes active, or return -1 if it is impossible for the string to become active.
constraints: The order array is a permutation of all string indices.
At time t, positions order[0] through order[t] become stars.
A substring is valid when it contains at least one star.
reference_solution:
def minimum_activation_time(s,order,k):
    n=len(s);total=n*(n+1)//2
    def active(time):
        starred=[False]*n
        for index in order[:time+1]:starred[index]=True
        invalid=run=0
        for index in range(n+1):
            if index<n and not starred[index]:run+=1
            else:invalid+=run*(run+1)//2;run=0
        return total-invalid>=k
    if not active(n-1):return -1
    low=0;high=n-1
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if active(middle):high=middle
        else:low=middle+1
    return low

hints: The number of valid substrings never decreases as more positions become stars.
Binary-search the first time whose valid-substring count reaches k.
For a candidate time, subtract star-free segment substring counts from n(n+1)/2.
Monotonicity makes the first passing time searchable, and every invalid substring lies in exactly one maximal star-free segment.
